close_reason: Folded into fz-kdt.34. Revision causality and formula identity are generic scheduler-owned telemetry, not an activation-specific prerequisite or second observation ledger.
description:
## Goal

Expose enough production telemetry to prove whether activation analysis behaves like a spreadsheet: an activation formula runs initially or because an exact input cell changed, and unchanged output stops propagation.

This is the measurement prerequisite for fz-kdt.13, not an optimization ticket.

## Current gap

The public fz.compiler2.job span identifies only the job kind, so 1,382 AnalyzeActivation runs cannot be grouped by activation key. The CLI telemetry stream also omits the activation-input, return-type, activation-analysis, and callsite movements needed to attribute each rerun to its changed ground.

## Output contract

For every AnalyzeActivation completion, public telemetry can determine:

- stable activation identity without hot-path display formatting;
- initial demand versus the exact read/wait revision movement that woke it;
- rebased or ordinary monotone ascent;
- which output fact keys semantically changed;
- which readers those changes woke;
- blocked versus concluded state.

Reuse the scheduler's authoritative dependency/revision state. Do not create a second telemetry-only dependency ledger or eagerly format compiler types.

## Acceptance

- A small activation chain proves every non-initial analysis has an unobserved dependency revision.
- An analysis with semantic-equivalent outputs records no changed output and wakes no downstream reader.
- Two runs of each target fixture yield identical per-activation evaluation/change histograms.
- enum_take_drop_split and fz_f98_range_map_converges can be reduced to distinct activation counts, evaluations per activation, changed-input causes, changed-output counts, and downstream wakes from the public log alone.
- Telemetry-disabled runs do not materialize display strings or cloned inventories.
- Documentation describes the fields and the change-proportional invariant.
title: Expose activation-cell identity and revision causality in public telemetry
